questions: Does oval progress stay at or above about 0.65 with the controller change, confirming that the 50 mm span is a stable base?
Do max_error excursions (about 0.059 to 0.064 m) start before or after a line-loss event, and at which bend types (s-bend, slalom) do they cluster?
What kp, ki and kd did you use at 50 mm, and did steering_oscillation stay near 0.2 to 0.3?
Is there any sign of the drivetrain limiting on the oval (finish time near 1.8 s), or is turn rate the limit once the controller is tuned?
If max_error stays at or above 0.06 m after your change, would you accept wheel_track 0.10 in the next iteration with no other geometry change?

intent: Hold the iteration 4 geometry (50 mm span, 12 mm footprint, y 0.05, unchanged body and drivetrain) so the Integrator's controller changes are the only variable in the next race. Expect oval progress of about 0.7 or higher, line losses of 1 to 1.4 per run, and max_error still near 0.06 m. If max_error stays on its plateau after the controller change, the next geometry test is wheel_track 0.10.
learning: Span is non-monotonic with progress: 40 mm gives 0.664, 50 mm gives 0.710, 60 mm gives 0.275 (both at 12 mm footprint). The optimum is near 50 mm. Footprint is secondary: at 60 mm, 16 mm gave 0.405 against 0.275 for 12 mm. Lead y 0.05 is required; y 0.03 collapses progress. max_error has stayed at 0.059 to 0.065 m in every iteration, so it is not explained by span, footprint or lead. Turn rate through wheel_track is the open question for it.
rationale:
Iteration 4 (50 mm span, 12 mm footprint, y 0.05) is the best design so far. Oval progress rose to 0.710 from 0.664 at 40 mm and 0.275 at 60 mm, and the score reached 188.0, with 3 of 20 oval runs finishing. Line losses stayed within the expected band (oval 1.2, s-bend 1.0, slalom 1.4), so the span is not losing the tape. Progress therefore peaks near 50 mm and does not keep rising toward 40 mm, so the Integrator's rule to move toward 40 mm does not apply. I keep the 50 mm span, 12 mm footprint and y 0.05 lead unchanged.

The remaining failure is off-track excursions. max_error sits at 0.0586 to 0.064 m against a 0.06 m limit. Body width cannot raise that limit: max(0.06, 0.0125 + body_width/4) is 0.06 m for any width in range, so I leave body_width at 0.12. Wheel_track is the only untested turn-rate lever, but changing it now would shift the effective steering gain by about 20 percent and confound the Integrator's controller tuning, which is already changing in this iteration. I therefore hold the geometry fixed so the next race isolates the controller change, and I flag wheel_track 0.10 as the next geometry test if max_error stays on its plateau.

Expected result: oval progress at or near 0.7, line losses 1 to 1.4, and max_error still around 0.06 m. Any gain should come from the controller.
